title: CRITICAL: Cross-context hashing not implemented in evaluate-preview; per-context isolation persists post-track
description:
The headline feature of flag_eval_unify_20260522 — cross-context percentage hashing — does NOT work in /flags/<key>/evaluate-preview.

Repro: rule with hash_inputs = [user.key, device.params.name, device.key, user.params.os, application.key]; preview request bundle = [user:alice, device:device-42 (os=iOS 18, name=iPhone-15-Pro), application:stitchd-web].

Expected: ALL three context results have identical hash_input = 'cross-ctx-test{env_id}aliceAlice Wonderlanddevice-42iOS 18stitchd-web' (or similar combining all 5 selectors), and identical bucket → identical variant.

Actual hash_input strings (from PUT /evaluate-preview response 94431.670):
- alice: 'cross-ctx-test{env_id}alice' (just user.key)
- device-42: 'cross-ctx-test{env_id}iPhone-15-Prodevice-42' (device.params.name + device.key)
- stitchd-web: 'cross-ctx-test{env_id}stitchd-web' (just application.key)

Each context's hash_input only includes selectors that match its own context_type. This is the OLD per-context behaviour — the unification's spec FR-1 + FR-2 explicitly requires the new evaluate_flag to take contexts:&[Context] as a BUNDLE and resolve selectors across all contexts.

Root cause hypothesis: flag-service's evaluate_preview handler is calling evaluate_flag once per context (single-context bundle each time), instead of one call with the full bundle. See worker P2's note: 'evaluate_preview calls evaluate_flag once per EvaluationContext and takes the first per-context result.' That's the bug — for cross-context hashing to work, the bundle must contain ALL contexts on every call.
notes:
Discovered during feature-flag-2cn manual UI bug-finding pass. This is THE bug — the track shipped without exercising cross-context hashing end-to-end via the actual preview UI. The Phase 8 worker's parity test used direct evaluate_flag calls (with multi-context bundles) which is why it passed; but the flag-service preview wrapper destroys the bundle.
FIXED: Cross-context hashing in evaluate-preview now works end-to-end.
COMMIT: 30dc683
FILES: crates/stitchd-core/src/evaluation/preview.rs, crates/stitchd-flag-service/src/service.rs, crates/stitchd-gateway/src/routes/flags.rs, crates/stitchd-flag-service/tests/{evaluate_preview_byte_equivalence,preview_cross_context_bundle}.rs, sdks/rust/tests/e2e_cross_context_hashing.rs
APPROACH: Gateway combines UI's flat Vec<Context> into ONE EvaluationContext bundle. core.evaluate_preview emits one result per sub-context in each bundle (was: one per bundle). All per-sub-context results share the same cross-context hash_input/bucket/variant. context_index is now a global flat index.
TESTS: multi_subcontext_bundle_shares_cross_context_hash_input + updated baseline_cross_context_hash and SDK preview-agree e2e for new N-results shape.
close_reason: Fixed (30dc683)

title: segment_scylla_20260516: Move list-based segment storage to ScyllaDB
design: Move list-based segment entries from PostgreSQL (segment_list_entries, pg_partman monthly partitions) to ScyllaDB to handle millions of rows per (segment_id, context_type). Hard cutover (greenfield). PG keeps segment metadata only. Storage layout: entries PK=(segment_id, context_type, generation), CK=(list_type, entry_key); separate pointer table maps (segment_id, context_type) → active_generation. Full-replace via generation-swap with LWT-protected CAS pointer flip. Diff-based add_entries/remove_entries for incremental edits. Drop the fetch-all-keys read path entirely (find_with_list removed, replaced with get_list_segment_summary counts; admin UI segment detail switches to counts + search-by-key Add/Remove). Use official scylla Rust driver with token-aware routing + prepared statements. Adds scylladb to docker-compose, CQL migration tooling, generation sweeper, Prometheus/OTel observability, and mdBook docs.
acceptance_criteria: PG segment_list_entries + pg_partman dropped via forward-only migration. scylladb in docker-compose with healthcheck; cargo test --workspace passes. crates/stitchd-db/scylla-migrations/ contains versioned CQL migrations. SegmentRepository exposes set_list_entries, add_entries, remove_entries, check_list_membership, batch_check_list_membership, find_memberships_batch, get_list_segment_summary; find_with_list removed. Property test confirms 100k-key generation-swap never shows mixed state to concurrent readers. LWT pointer flip prevents concurrent-replace corruption. Sweeper integration test removes orphaned generations after retention window. Admin UI detail page shows counts + Add/Remove search-by-key; no fetch-all. gRPC GetSegment for list segments returns summary. Prometheus exposes Scylla metrics; OTel includes Scylla spans. conductor/tech-stack.md + mdBook docs updated. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes. tarpaulin coverage ≥90% for stitchd-db and stitchd-segmentation-service.

title: Flag evaluator's InSegment leaf returns false for LIST-based segments even when user is in include list
design: When a flag rule has Leaf{InSegment:<list_segment_id>}, the flag-service evaluator always returns false regardless of whether the context key is in the segment's include list. Rule-based segment InSegment works correctly. Reproduce on dark-mode-beta flag: rule {country==US AND InSegment(BetaTesters)} → no_match for alice@acme.com even though direct segmentation-service /v1/segments/{id}/entries/lookup?key=alice@acme.com returns {in_include:true,in_exclude:false}. Switching the segment to PowerUsers (rule-based, tier==premium) makes the same flag rule match correctly. So the bug is specifically in the flag-evaluator's path to check list-segment membership — likely either (a) not calling segmentation-service.EvaluateMembership with the right env_id/context, or (b) using an in-process cache that never gets the Scylla entries, or (c) the segmentation client returns a default-false on some specific error condition. Look in crates/stitchd-flag-service/src/evaluator/ for the InSegment leaf handler and trace its membership-check codepath for list-type segments.
acceptance_criteria: POST /v1/projects/{proj}/flags/{key}/evaluate-preview with a context whose key is in a list-based segment's include returns fired_rule_index pointing at the rule whose InSegment leaf references that segment. Specifically: alice@acme.com (in BetaTesters include) + country=US triggers rule 0 (variant=on) when rule 0 is {And:[Eq(country,US), InSegment(BetaTesters)]}.
notes:
COMPLETED: InSegment for list-based segments always returned false — fixed by wiring CompositeSegmentRepository in flag-service and adding pre_resolved_list_memberships to evaluate_preview
COMMIT: 3f4847b
ROOT CAUSE: (1) fetch_segment_definitions skipped all List-type segments with a placeholder comment; (2) PgSegmentRepository.find_memberships_batch queried the dropped segment_list_entries Postgres table instead of Scylla
FILES: crates/stitchd-core/src/evaluation/preview.rs, crates/stitchd-flag-service/src/main.rs, crates/stitchd-flag-service/src/service.rs

title: Bug: UI allows saving a rule with NO WHEN conditions; rule silently becomes 'match-all' without explicit user acknowledgement
description: After removing all WHEN clauses from a rule (clicking the X on the empty default Eq), the rule editor lets the user click 'Save rules' and saves a rule with condition=And[] (empty). Either: (a) require at least one condition (block save with 'Add at least one WHEN condition'), or (b) add an explicit 'Match all contexts' checkbox/toggle that the user must enable to commit to no conditions. title: Bug: Saving a rule injects a second auto-generated 'default fallthrough' rule with And:[] condition; UI shows 1 but API has 2
description: After saving 1 user-authored rule on a percentage flag, the API returns 2 rules: (1) the user's rule with cross-context hash_inputs, (2) an auto-injected rule {condition: And[], output: variant_key:'off'}. The 'Targeting' tab badge counts both (shows 2), but the rule list UI only renders the user-authored rule. The 'default' should live in flag.default_variant_id / default_variant_key — flag.default_variant_key is null on this saved flag. The auto-injected rule is a workaround that bypasses the canonical default field.
notes:
Reproduces on first rule save. Discovered during feature-flag-2cn. Likely fix: either (a) move the catch-all to default_variant_key on PUT, or (b) suppress it from the UI count + render but acknowledge it's a back-end artifact.
FIXED: Server-side normalisation strips trailing And:[] catch-all rule and absorbs its output into default_variant_id / default_rule_distribution.
COMMIT: 8f483c2
FILES: crates/stitchd-flag-service/src/service.rs
APPROACH: In MutateFlag(Update), when flag_proto.default_variant_key is empty AND the inbound rules list's LAST entry has condition == And:[] (the always-true sentinel), the catch-all's output is absorbed into record.default_variant_id (VariantKey output) or record.default_rule_distribution (PercentageAllocation output, weights converted milli→percentage with RolloutDistribution::validate). The catch-all rule is stripped from the persisted list, so GET responses now show exactly the user-authored rules.
TESTS: service::tests::mutate_flag_update_strips_trailing_catch_all_rule_into_default_variant; service::tests::mutate_flag_update_keeps_non_catch_all_trailing_rule (sanity — non-empty conditions are NOT stripped)
close_reason: Fixed (8f483c2)

title: Bug: Rule saved with empty WHEN clause submits literal Eq{param:'',value:''} that never matches
description: When the user clicks 'Add first rule' and configures only Serve/Hash inputs (no WHEN condition), the rule editor pre-populates a default ConditionExpr.Leaf(Eq{context_type:'user',param:'',value:''}) and silently saves it. Saved rule body shows: condition = And[Leaf(Eq{context_type:'user',param:'',value:''})]. Since no context has an empty-string param/value, this rule will NEVER fire. The UI shows no error and the rule appears 'saved'. Either: (a) reject save with 'WHEN attribute is required' error, or (b) omit the empty Eq from the saved condition (treat as 'always match').
notes:
Reproduces on every rule create. Discovered during feature-flag-2cn. Saved payload: see request 94431.514 PUT /rules response. Fix likely in ConditionClauseEditor.tsx / RuleCard.tsx / EditFlagDefaultRule.helpers.ts where the default ConditionExpr is constructed.
FIXED: Server-side defense-in-depth validation rejects empty Eq leaf in saved rule conditions.
COMMIT: 3025033
FILES: crates/stitchd-flag-service/src/mapping.rs, crates/stitchd-flag-service/src/service.rs
APPROACH: New mapping::validate_proto_rule_condition walks the deserialised ConditionExpr; flags any Leaf(Eq) where param == "" AND value == Str(""). Wired into MutateFlag(Update) right after the existing hash_inputs validation. Returns Status::invalid_argument with the 'invalid_condition' sentinel.

title: Exploration: verify rollout-hash docs against implementation (key vs param per context)
notes:
WISP DIGEST — Percentage allocation doc/code audit.
SUMMARY: The doc snippet in docs/src/architecture/evaluation-flow.md:138 is wrong on 6 points AND glosses over the fact that the SDK (sdks/rust/src/client.rs::compute_allocation, murmur3) and the server rule engine (crates/stitchd-core/src/rule_engine/percentage.rs::allocate_percentage, SipHasher13) use DIFFERENT hash functions, DIFFERENT input formats, and DIFFERENT included fields (only the server includes project_id). Same context routes to different variants on SDK vs server preview.
DOC BUGS: (1) hash input shape claims BOTH key AND params concat'd, real SDK does XOR per ctx_type; (2) project_id is NOT in the SDK hash; (3) bucket space is 0..999 not 0..99999; (4) weight_milli sums to 1000 not 100_000; (5) 'Three hash families configurable via UpdateFlagHashing' — no such API, hash fn is hardcoded; (6) 'preview == SDK' claim is false.
REQUIREMENT GAP: The proto ContextHashSpec model can NOT express 'key AND param for the same context type' — empty/non-empty parameter_names is a XOR. Server-side PercentageTarget Vec model CAN. If product wants per-context combos, proto needs an include_key bool field.
close_reason: Doc audit complete; findings recorded. Not fixing inline — see digest for the recommended changes.

title: CH 24 new analyzer: arrayExists(...) in JOIN ON fails on stats-service queries
description:
stitchd-stats-service::queries::{aggregation,ratio,funnel,preview} all express the events_v2 -> experiment_assignments join with arrayExists(t -> t.1 = a.context_type AND t.2 = a.context_key, e.contexts) in the JOIN ON clause.

When run against a live ClickHouse 24 instance with the experimental analyzer ON (the future default), the join loses joined-table column qualification: errors like 'Not found column __table2.context_type in block __table1.env_id UUID UUID...'.

With the legacy analyzer (allow_experimental_analyzer = 0): 'Unsupported JOIN ON conditions. INVALID_JOIN_ON_EXPRESSION'.

Phase 11 E2E (experiment_lifecycle_e2e.rs) sidesteps this with ARRAY JOIN of contexts followed by a plain equi-join on (env_id, ctx_type, ctx_key). Same semantics, no analyzer trap.

ACCEPTANCE: rewrite build_aggregation_query, build_ratio_query, build_funnel_query, and build_experiment_preview_aggregation_query to use ARRAY JOIN on contexts first, then a plain equi-join. Verify via the existing #[ignore]d integration tests in stitchd-stats-service/tests/. Update the bind-order test if any binds shift.
notes:
FIXED: all 4 production query builders rewritten to ARRAY JOIN. Live-CH execution tests added (previously SQL-string-only; UUID serde annotations were also missing — fixed at the same time). New multi-context-type funnel integration test asserts ('user', ...) + ('account', ...) tuples attribute to both assignment rows.
COMMITS: 7a17cfa (aggregation) 29116d6 (ratio) 62495ba (funnel) 2f23ae1 (preview) 64309fe (verification checkpoint)

title: Gateway: AdminFlagJson.rules missing rule_id + name fields

The gateway's AdminFlagJson.rules (crates/stitchd-gateway/src/routes/flags.rs::RuleJson) serialises {name, condition, output, segment_ids} but does NOT include the underlying feature_flag_rules.id UUID nor surface the 'name' field consistently.

LEARNINGS:
- Legacy aggregate BayesianResult (in stats::mod) is retained for the existing analyze_count/analyze_numeric/analyze_funnel/analyze_percentile callers used by recommendation.rs. The new per-variant BayesianVariantResult lives in bayesian.rs and is what UI/results JSON will consume — separate types prevent the two integration paths from drifting.
- Deterministic 10k-MC with a fixed seed (0x00C0_FFEE_5EED — note: clippy::unusual_byte_groupings requires hex literal groups of 4) gives tight per-call reproducibility. PtB Monte Carlo error is ~0.005; the 'modest lift' test uses a wide (0.7, 0.9) interval to absorb that.
- Normal-Normal weak-prior approximation: post_var = sample_var / n; difference posterior is N(mean_t - mean_c, post_var_c + post_var_t). PtB via 1 - Φ(-diff/diff_se) reusing the existing normal_cdf helper. The +1σ test mathematically constructs diff = sqrt(diff_var) so PtB = Φ(1).

title: Track API only accepts one context per event — storage already supports many
description:
Bug: the SDK / admin-track wire format takes a single (context_type, context_key) pair per TrackEvent, but the ClickHouse row and the core EventPayload both model contexts as Array<Tuple<String,String>>. Result: an event that's attributable to multiple contexts (e.g. purchase_completed → user:alice + account:acme + session:s99) cannot be expressed correctly. Splitting into N events 3x-inflates count metrics; picking one drops attribution dimensions.

Affected surfaces (all singular):
- proto/analytics/v1/analytics.proto lines 17-18, 46-48, 93-94 (TrackEvent + admin-track variant + EventFiring)
- crates/stitchd-gateway/src/routes/events.rs:40-41, 78-79, 319-321, 369-370 (request/response DTOs)
- crates/stitchd-analytics-service/src/grpc/ingestion.rs:311 (wraps singular into 1-element vec)
- admin/src/pages/events/TestEventWidget.tsx:50-51, 77-78, 178-179, 247-248, 255-256, 359-366

Fix shape (suggested):
- Change TrackEvent.context_type + context_key to repeated EventContext (proto)
- Backwards compat: keep singular fields as 'first context' fallback for one release if external SDKs depend on them; new field is contexts: repeated EventContext
- Threads through gateway DTO → ingestion → drops the vec! wrapping at ingestion.rs:311
- Admin TestEventWidget gets a FieldArray<EventContext> like CreateMetricModal funnel-steps.
close_reason: Wire format now accepts repeated EventContext on TrackEvent + EventFiring; ingestion handler prefers contexts[] with fallback to singular for SDK compat. Admin TestEventWidget rebuilt with FieldArray. Verified end-to-end via curl + UI. 6 new tests + 144/200/96 backend/gateway/admin tests still pass. Commit 4a08661.

title: extend SDK polling to fetch event_definitions
description: The Rust SDK Client::track() (Phase 5 Task 5.2, commit pending) ships with an empty event_definitions cache in DefinitionSnapshot. This means every track() call currently warns + skips because no event_key is registered. To make track() useful in production, the polling layer must fetch event definitions alongside flags and seed snapshot.event_definitions on each sync.
design:
Two options:
1. **Extend SyncDefinitions proto** — add 'repeated EventDefinitionMeta event_definitions = 6;' to SyncDefinitionsResponse. EventDefinitionMeta carries {event_key, value_type} only (no env_id/version metadata — SDK doesn't need those). Gateway populates it from PG event_definitions on each call.
2. **New dedicated RPC** — 'rpc SyncEventDefinitions(SyncEventDefinitionsRequest) returns (SyncEventDefinitionsResponse);' on a separate poll cycle.

Option (1) is simpler and reuses the existing definition_poll_interval. Modify:
- proto/sdk/v1/service.proto (add EventDefinitionMeta + field)
- crates/stitchd-gateway routes/sdk_sync.rs (populate from PG)
- sdks/rust/src/snapshot.rs DefinitionSnapshot::from_proto (read into event_definitions map)
- sdks/rust/src/client.rs GrpcDefinitionFetcher::fetch (no changes — proto generation does it)

TDD: snapshot test that from_proto populates event_definitions; integration test that polling end-to-end populates the cache.
notes: Marked TODO in sdks/rust/src/snapshot.rs::DefinitionSnapshot::event_definitions doc comment. Until this is implemented, Client::track() is effectively disabled in production (warn + skip everything). Tests use DefinitionSnapshot::with_event_definitions to seed manually.

title: evaluate-preview rule_traces.conditions array is empty — should contain per-leaf evaluation results
design: POST /v1/projects/{project}/flags/{flag}/evaluate-preview returns rule_traces with rule_index + outcome, but the per-rule 'conditions' array (intended for granular leaf-by-leaf trace) is always empty. Reproduce: create a flag with an AND of multiple conditions (e.g. Eq + InSegment + InSegment), enable it, POST evaluate-preview. Response includes rule_traces=[{rule_index:0,outcome:'no_match',conditions:[]},...] — but conditions:[] regardless of input. Likely a gap in the flag-service evaluate_preview handler not emitting per-leaf traces. The frontend's PreviewTab probably expects these for the rule-builder UI's 'why didn't this match' explanations.

title: Phantom empty Eq condition in segment rule editor — first Add condition pre-populates a zero-value clause
design: When opening the PowerUsers (rule-based) segment detail and clicking 'Add condition' for the first time, the rule editor inserts TWO leaves: an empty {Eq:{param:'',value:'',context_type:'user'}} followed by the user's actual condition. The empty leaf nullifies the entire rule because no context has an empty-name parameter. Affects segment rule builder; not seen in flag rule builder so it's specific to SegmentDetail's rule editor mount. Reproduce: create a fresh rule-based segment, open detail, click 'Add condition', set attribute=tier value=premium, Save. condition_expr in PG will contain both an empty leaf and the real one.
acceptance_criteria: Adding the first condition to a fresh rule-based segment produces exactly ONE leaf in condition_expr. No phantom empty Eq.

title: docs_refresh_20260522: Docs Refresh & Autogeneration Pipeline
design: Two-pronged: (1) Extend existing crates/xtask/src/main.rs with env-vars scraper, cargo-rdme integration, and broken-link checker; layer on top of existing proto-gen + OpenAPI-export + SDK-rustdoc + mdbook-build steps. (2) One-shot bulk rewrite of stale narrative pages (introduction, architecture/*, gateway/*, deployment/* minus generated env-vars, sdk/README) against current code via parallel workers grouped by topic. Phase 3 runs 5 workers concurrently with explicit file-ownership boundaries per workflow.md. Idempotency enforced via 'cargo xtask docs && git diff --exit-code' CI job.
acceptance_criteria: 1) cargo xtask docs runs idempotent (no diff on second run). 2) mdbook build docs/ succeeds with zero broken-link warnings. 3) Every code reference in every rewritten page resolves to a live symbol. 4) docs/src/internal/* orphans deleted. 5) All crates/*/README.md regenerated from rustdoc, preamble standardized. 6) New CI docs job runs xtask + git-diff-exit-code. 7) No CI regressions.
